1619.subject: Physics
1619.text: An electron is travelling along the $x$-direction. It encounters a magnetic field in the $y$-direction. Its subsequent motion will be
options: a circle in the $x z$ plane
a circle in the $y z$ plane
a circle in the $x y$ plane.
1619.sol:
We know that the force on a charged particle $e$ due to a magnetic field is given by

$ \begin{array}{ll} 
& \vec{F}=e(\vec{v} \times \vec{B}) \\
\text{ Here } \vec{v}=v_x=\hat{i} \text{ and } \vec{B}=B_y \hat{j} \\
\therefore \quad & \vec{F}=e v_x B_y(\hat{i} \times \hat{j})=e v_x B_y \hat{k}
\end{array} $
Therefore the subsequent motion of the charged particle will be a circle in the $x z$ plane.

1806.subject: Physics
1806.text: A solid cylinder, a circular disc, a solid sphere and a hollow cylinder of the same radius are placed on an inclined plane. Which of the following will have maximum acceleration at the bottom of the plane?
1806.sol:
Let the inclination of the inclined plane be $\theta$. Acceleration of a rolling body is given as
$a=\frac{g \sin \theta}{\left(1+K^2 / R^2\right)}$ Here, $K$ is radius of gyration. For circular disc $I=\frac{1}{2} M R^2 \quad \therefore \frac{K^2}{R^2}=\frac{1}{2}$ $\therefore \quad a=\frac{2}{3} g \sin \theta$
For solid cylinder $I=\frac{1}{2} M R^2 \therefore \frac{K^2}{R^2}=\frac{1}{2}$ $\therefore \quad a=\frac{2}{3} g \sin \theta$
For solid sphere $I=\frac{2}{5} M R^2 \therefore \frac{K^2}{R^2}=\frac{2}{5}$ $\therefore \quad a=\frac{5}{7} g \sin \theta$
For hollow cylinder $I=M R^2 \quad \therefore \frac{K^2}{R^2}=1$ $\therefore a=\frac{1}{2} g \sin \theta$
Hence, from (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv) we conclude that the solid sphere will reach the bottom with maximum acceleration.

4565.text:
Identify correct statements from the following:
i. \(\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{BO}_{3}\) is a monobasic acid.
ii. The correct formula of borax is \(\mathrm{Na}_{2}\left[\mathrm{ B}_{4} \mathrm{O}_{5}( \mathrm{OH})_3\right] 8 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}\).
iii. $\mathrm{NaBH}_{4}$ is a reducing agent.
4565.sol:
The explanations of given statements are as follows : (i) \($\mathrm{H}}_{3} \mathrm{BO}$}_{3}\) is a monobasic acid because in aqueous solution, it coordinates with a molecule of water to form a hydrated species,
\(\mathrm{B}^{3+}\) ion pulls the \($\sigma$\)-electron charge of coordinated \($\mathrm{O}$\)-atom towards itself. The coordinated oxygen, in turn, pull the \($\sigma$\)-electrons of \($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$\) bond of the attached water molecule towards itself. This facilitates the removal of \(\mathrm{H}^{+}\)ion from the \($\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}$\) bond. It can be written as follows: \($\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_$3+$\mathrm{H}}_{2} \mathrm{O} \rightleftharpoons\left[\mathrm{B}(\mathrm{OH})_4 \Gamma+\mathrm{H}^{+}\right.\) (ii) The correct formula for borax is \(\mathrm{Na}$}_{2}$\left[\mathrm{~B}}_{4} \mathrm{O}$}_{7}\right] $\cdot$10 $\mathrm{H}}_{2} $\mathrm{O}$\). (iii) \(\mathrm{NaBH}$}_{4}\) is a selective reducing agent for aldehydes, ketones and ester. Thus, statements (i) and (iii) are correct.

4920.subject: Chemistry
4920.text:
Identify the reactions in which dichromate acts as an oxidising reagent.
I. $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}+6 \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}+14 \mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+6 \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+7 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
II. $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
III. $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}+6 \mathrm{I}^{-}+14 \mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+3 \mathrm{I}_2+7 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
IV. $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7+2 \mathrm{KCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7+2 \mathrm{NaCl}$
4920.sol:
In reaction I and III, dichromate acts as an oxidising reagent.
(I) $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}+6 \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}+14 \mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+6 \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}+7 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
In the above reaction, $\mathrm{Cr}^{6+}$ reduced to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ oxidised to $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$.
(II) $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{CrO}_4^{2-}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
In the above reaction, there is no change occuring in the oxidation state of $\mathrm{Cr}$.
(III) $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}+6 \mathrm{I}^{-}+14 \mathrm{H}^{+} \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{Cr}^{3+} +3 \mathrm{I}_2+7 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$
In the above reaction, $\mathrm{Cr}^{6+}$ has reduced to $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ has oxidised to $\mathrm{I}_2$.
(IV) $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7+2 \mathrm{KCl} \longrightarrow \mathrm{K}_2 \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7+2 \mathrm{NaCl}$
In the above reaction, no change in the oxidation state of $\mathrm{Cr}$ has taken place.

5499.subject: Chemistry
5499.text: At same temperature and pressure, the rate of diffusion of gas ' $X$ ' is $3 \sqrt{3}$ times that of a gaseous hydrocarbon of molar mass $54 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}$. The molar mass of $X$ in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ is
5499.sol:
According to Graham's law of diffusion rate of diffusion of a gas is inversely proportional to square root of its density.

$\text{ Rate } \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\text{ Density }}}$ But, density of the gas is proportional to its molar mass, thus
Rate of diffusion $\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M_m}}$
For two gases we have

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{ Rate }_1}{\text{ Rate }_2}& =\sqrt{\frac{M_{m_2}}{M_{m_1}}}\\
\left(\frac{\text{ Rate }_1}{\text{ Rate }_2}\right)^2 & =\frac{M_{m_2}}{M_{m_1}}\\
M_{m_2} & =\left(\frac{\text{ Rate }_1}{\text{ Rate }_2}\right)^2 M_{m_1} \\
& =\left(\frac{1}{3 \sqrt{3}}\right)^2 \times54 \\
& =\frac{1}{9 \times 3} \times54 \\
& =\frac{54}{27}=2 \mathrm{ g} \mathrm{ mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$

7855.sol:

Let, $I_1=\int_{-\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{x}{2-\cos ^2 x} d xf(x)=\frac{x}{2-\cos ^2 x}f(-x)=\frac{-x}{2-\cos 2(-x)}=\frac{-x}{2-\cos 2 x}=-f(x)f(x)$ is an odd function.
Thus, $I_1=0$
Let $I_1=\frac{\pi}{4} \int_{-\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{1}{2-\cos 2 x} d xg(x)=\frac{\pi}{4(2-\cos 2 x)}g(-x)=\frac{\pi}{4(2-\cos 2(-x))}=\frac{\pi}{4(2-\cos 2 x)}=g(x)\therefore \quad g(x)$ is an even function

Now, $\mathrm{I}=\mathrm{I}_2=\frac{\pi}{4} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{d x}{2-\frac{1-\tan ^2 x}{1+\tan ^2 x}}\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\pi}{4} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{1+\tan ^2 x}{2+\tan ^2 x-1+\tan ^2 x} d x \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\pi}{4} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{\sec ^2 x}{1+3 \tan ^2 x} d x
\end{aligned}$
Put $\tan x=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 x d x=d t$
Limits : $x=0 \quad \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=0\begin{aligned}
& x=\frac{\pi}{4} \quad \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=1 \\
& \therefore \quad \mathrm{I}=\frac{\pi}{4} \int_0^1 \frac{d t}{1+3 t^2} \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\pi}{2} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left[\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{3} t\right]_0^1 \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{3}}\left[\tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{3})-\tan ^{-1}(0)\right] \\
& \mathrm{I}=\frac{\pi}{2 \sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=\frac{\pi^2}{6 \sqrt{3}}
\end{aligned}$

19742.subject: Chemistry
19742.text: The number of bond pairs and lone pairs of electrons in the molecule $\text{IF}_5$ is:
19742.sol:
The central atom in $\text{IF}_5$ is Iodine (I).

Number of valence electrons in Iodine = $7$.

Number of Fluorine atoms bonded to Iodine = $5$.

Each Fluorine atom forms a single bond with Iodine, so the number of bond pairs = $5$.

Number of valence electrons used in bonding = $5$.

Remaining valence electrons on Iodine = $7 - 5 = 2$.

Number of lone pairs = $\dfrac{2}{2} = 1$.

Thus, the molecule $\text{IF}_5$ has $5$ bond pairs and $1$ lone pair.

Answer: $5, 1$

20657.subject: Chemistry
20657.text: A solute $\mathrm{X}$ is found to exist as a dimer in water. A 4 molal solution of $\mathrm{X}$ shows a boiling point of $101.04^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$. What is the percentage association of $\mathrm{X}$ ? ($\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}$ for water $=0.52 \mathrm{ K} / \mathrm{m}$).
20657.sol:
The elevation in boiling point is given by $\Delta T_b = T_b - T_b^{{}^{\circ}} = 101.04^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C} - 100^{{}^{\circ}} \text{C} = 1.04 \text{ K}$.

Using the formula $\Delta T_b = i K_b m$, where $i$ is the van't Hoff factor, $K_b = 0.52 \text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$, and $m = 4 \text{ m}$:

$1.04 = i \times 0.52 \times 4$

$i = \dfrac{1.04}{2.08} = 0.5$.

For the dimerization of solute X, the reaction is $2X \rightarrow X_2$. If $\alpha$ is the degree of association, the van't Hoff factor is given by $i = 1 - \alpha + \dfrac{\alpha}{n}$, where $n=2$ for a dimer.

$0.5 = 1 - \alpha + \dfrac{\alpha}{2}$

$0.5 = 1 - \dfrac{\alpha}{2}$

$\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = 0.5$

$\alpha = 1$.

The percentage association is $\alpha \times 100 = 1 \times 100 = 100\%$.

Answer: 100

21244.subject: Mathematics
21244.sol:
Let $I = \int_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} \dfrac{1}{1 + \sqrt{\tan x}} dx$.

Using the property $\int_a^{b} f(x) dx = \int_a^{b} f(a + b - x) dx$, we have $a + b = \dfrac{\pi}{6} + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

$I = \int_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} \dfrac{1}{1 + \sqrt{\tan(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - x)}} dx = \int_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} \dfrac{1}{1 + \sqrt{\cot x}} dx$.

$I = \int_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} \dfrac{1}{1 + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\tan x}}} dx = \int_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} \dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{\sqrt{\tan x} + 1} dx$.

Adding the two expressions for $I$:

$2I = \int_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} \left( \dfrac{1}{1 + \sqrt{\tan x}} + \dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{1 + \sqrt{\tan x}} \right) dx = \int_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} 1 dx$.

$2I = [x]_{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}^{\dfrac{\pi}{3}} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{12}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{12}$

21514.subject: Mathematics
21514.text: Given that $f(x)=k x^3-9 k x^2+9 x+3$ is an increasing function on R set of real numbers, then $k$ belongs to
21514.sol:
The function $f(x) = kx^3 - 9kx^2 + 9x + 3$ is increasing on $\mathbb{R}$ if and only if its derivative $f'(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

Calculating the derivative:
$f'(x) = 3kx^2 - 18kx + 9$.

For $f'(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$, the quadratic expression $3kx^2 - 18kx + 9$ must satisfy two conditions:
1. The coefficient of $x^2$ must be positive, so $3k > 0$, which implies $k > 0$.
2. The discriminant $D$ must be less than or equal to zero, so $D \le 0$.

Calculating the discriminant $D = b^2 - 4ac$:
$D = (-18k)^2 - 4(3k)(9) = 324k^2 - 108k$.

Setting $D \le 0$:
$324k^2 - 108k \le 0$
$108k(3k - 1) \le 0$.

Since $k > 0$, we divide by $108k$ to get:
$3k - 1 \le 0$
$3k \le 1$
$k \le \dfrac{1}{3}$.

Combining $k > 0$ and $k \le \dfrac{1}{3}$, we get $k \in \left(0, \dfrac{1}{3}\right].

Answer: \left(0, \dfrac{1}{3}\right]$

21847.subject: Mathematics
21847.text: In a 12 storey house, 10 people enter a lift cabin. It is known that they will leave the lift in pre-decided groups of 2, 3 & 5 people at different storeys. The number of ways they can do so if the lift does not stop up to the second storey is
21847.sol:
The total number of storeys available is 12. Since the lift does not stop at the first and second storeys, the available storeys for the groups to exit are from the 3rd to the 12th storey. This gives $12 - 2 = 10$ available storeys.

There are 3 groups of people consisting of 2, 3, and 5 individuals. These groups must exit at different storeys. We need to select 3 distinct storeys out of the 10 available storeys and assign the groups to them.

The number of ways to choose 3 storeys out of 10 is ^{10}C_{3} = $\dfrac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{3 \times 2 \times 1} =120$.

Once the 3 storeys are chosen, the 3 distinct groups (size 2, 3, and 5) can be arranged in these 3 storeys in 3!$ ways.

Total number of ways = ^{10}C_{3} \times 3! = 120 \times 6 = 720$.

Answer: 720

&=8 \%+4 \%=12 \%
\end{aligned}
$

Statement I : In ${Cl}_{2}$ molecule the covalent radius is double of the atomic radius of chlorine.

Statement II : Radius of anionic species is always greater than their parent atomic radius.

Choose the most appropriate answer from options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
28548.sol:
In ${Cl}_{2}$ molecule, the covalent radius is half of the internuclear distance, so statement $\left(I\right)$ is false. The covalent radius is little smaller than the actual radius of the atom of chlorine due to overlapping during formation of covalent bond.

For the same element, anion has lower effective nuclear charge than atom so, anion is larger than the parent atom. That means statement $\left(II\right)$ is correct.

Reverberatory furnace, in copper, tin, and nickel production, a furnace used for smelting or refining in which the fuel is not in direct contact with the ore but heats it by a flame blown over it from another chamber.Purification of aluminium by electrolytic refining is known as Hoope's process. 30904.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The electronegativity of group $14$ elements from $Si$ to $Pb$ gradually decreases.

Statement II : Group $14$ contains non-metallic, metallic, as well as metalloid elements.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
30904.sol:
$Gr - 14EN$

$C2 . 5$

$Si1 . 8$

$Ge1 . 8$

$Sn1 . 8$

$Pb1 . 9$

The electronegativity values for elements from $Si$ to $Pb$ are almost same. So Statement I is false.

  1. Among them, Carbon and silicon are non-metals.
  2. Germanium is metalloid in nature
  3. Tin and lead are metal.

Reason for different metallic characteristics

  1. The metallic character increases down the group from carbon to lead as nonmetal to metal.
  2. The metallic character increases because the atomic size increases from Carbon to Lead.
  3. As size increases, the ionization potential decreases down the group.
  4. A decrease in ionization potential lead to an increase in the electropositive character of the element.

Hence, the metallic character increases down the group in group$- 14$ as the ionization potential decreases to make it easier to lose an electron and increase the metallic character.

32862.subject: Mathematics
32862.text: Let $M$ and $N$ be the number of points on the curve ${y}^{5} - 9xy + 2x = 0$, where the tangents to the curve are parallel to $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively. Then the value of $M + N$ equals _______.
32862.sol:
Given,

${y}^{5} - 9xy + 2x = 0 . . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now differentiating both side we get,

$5{y}^{4}\dfrac{dy}{x} - 9x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - 9y + 2 = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx}\left(5{y}^{4} - 9x\right) = 9y - 2$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{9y - 2}{5{y}^{4} - 9x} = 0 . . . . . \left(2\right)$

$⇒ 9y - 2 = 0$ (for horizontal tangent)

$⇒ y = \dfrac{2}{9}$, which does not satisfy the original equation so $M = 0$.

As ${\left(\dfrac{2}{9}\right)}^{5} - 9x \times \dfrac{2}{9} + 2x = 0$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{2}{9}\right)}^{5} - 2x + 2x = 0$

$⇒ {\left(\dfrac{2}{9}\right)}^{5} = 0\left\{\text{which is a false statement}\right\}$

Now $5{y}^{4} - 9x = 0$ (from equation $\left(2\right)$ for vertical tangent)

$⇒ 5{y}^{4}\left(9y - 2\right) - 9{y}^{5} = 0$ (putting the value of $x$ from equation $\left(1\right)$)

$⇒ {y}^{4}\left[45y - 10 - 9y\right] = 0$

$⇒ y = 0$ or $36y = 10$$⇒ y = \dfrac{5}{18}$

So at $y = 0 ⇒ x = 0$ and $y = \dfrac{5}{18} ⇒ x = {x}_{1}$

$\begin{cases}\left(0, 0\right) & \left({x}_{1}, \dfrac{5}{18}\right)\end{cases}$ (where ${x}_{1} = \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{5}{18}\right)}^{5}}{9 \times \dfrac{5}{18} - 2}$)

So, $N = 2$

$M + N = 0 + 2 = 2$

33601.text: Let the point $\left(p, p + 1\right)$ lie inside the region $E = \left\{\left(x, y\right): 3 - x \le y \le \sqrt{9 - {x}^{2}}, 0 \le x \le 3\right\} .$ If the set of all values of $p$ is the interval $\left(a, b\right),$ then ${b}^{2} + b - {a}^{2}$ is equal to $________ .$
33601.sol:
Given,

The point $\left(p, p + 1\right)$ lie inside the region $E = \left\{\left(x, y\right): 3 - x \le y \le \sqrt{9 - {x}^{2}}, 0 \le x \le 3\right\}$,

And the set of all values of $p$ is the interval $\left(a, b\right),$

Now by observation $\left(p, p + 1\right)$ lies on $y - x = 1$,

Also point $\left(p, p + 1\right)$ lies on $x + y = 3$

So, solving $y - x = 1$ and $x + y = 3$ we get, $P\left(1, 2\right)$

Again given point $\left(p, p + 1\right)$ lies on ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 9$

So, solving $y - x = 1$ and ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 9$, we get

${x}^{2} + ( 1 + x{)}^{2} = 9$

$⇒ 2{x}^{2} + 2x - 8 = 0$

$⇒ {x}^{2} + x - 4 = 0 . . . . . . . . . \left(i\right)$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 4 \cdot 4}}{2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 1}{2}$

Hence, $p \in \left(1, \dfrac{\sqrt{17} - 1}{2}\right)$

Now on comparing with $p \in \left(a, b\right)$ we get,

$⇒ a = 1, {b}^{2} + b = 4$ [using $\left(i\right)$]

Hence, the value of ${b}^{2} + b - {a}^{2} = 4 - 1 = 3$

35409.subject: Mathematics
35409.text: If the maximum distance of normal to the ellipse $\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1, b < 2$, from the origin is $1$ , then the eccentricity of the ellipse is:
35409.sol:
Given:

$\dfrac{{x}^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}} = 1$

Equation of normal to the ellipse is

$2xsec\theta - bycosec\theta = 4 - {b}^{2}$

Distance of normal from origin is

$d = \left|\dfrac{4 - {b}^{2}}{\sqrt{4{sec}^{2}\theta + {b}^{2}{cosec}^{2}\theta}}\right|$

For maximum distance, denominator must be minimum.

$\sqrt{4{sec}^{2}\theta + {b}^{2}{cosec}^{2}\theta}$

$= \sqrt{4 + 4\tan^{2}\theta + {b}^{2} + {b}^{2}{cot}^{2}\theta}$

Now,

$\dfrac{4\tan^{2}\theta + {b}^{2}{cot}^{2}\theta}{2} \ge \sqrt{4\tan^{2}\theta \times {b}^{2}{cot}^{2}\theta}$

$⇒ 4\tan^{2}\theta + {b}^{2}{cot}^{2}\theta \ge 4b$

$⇒ 4 + {b}^{2} + 4\tan^{2}\theta + {b}^{2}{cot}^{2}\theta \ge 4 + {b}^{2} + 4b$

$⇒ 4 + {b}^{2} + 4\tan^{2}\theta + {b}^{2}{cot}^{2}\theta \ge {\left(2 + b\right)}^{2}$

So, minimum value of $\sqrt{4{sec}^{2}\theta + {b}^{2}{cosec}^{2}\theta}$ is $\sqrt{{\left(2 + b\right)}^{2}} = b + 2$

So,

$d = \left|\dfrac{4 - {b}^{2}}{2 + b}\right| = 1$

$⇒ \left|2 - b\right| = 1$

$⇒ 2 - b = \pm 1$

$⇒ b = 1, 3$

But $b < 2$, so $b = 1$, hence

$e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

35497.text: For $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \delta \in \mathbb{N}$, if $∫ \left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right){\log}_{e}xdx = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{\betax} - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}{\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{\deltax} + C$, where $e = \mathop{∑}_{n = 0}^{\infty}\dfrac{1}{n !}$ and $C$ is constant of integration, then $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta$ is equal to
35497.sol:
Given,

$∫ \left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{\betax} - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}{\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{\deltax} + C$

Now let $I = ∫ \left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} + {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right)lnxdx$

Now let ${\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} = t$

$⇒ 2x\left(lnx - 1\right) = lnt$

$⇒ lnxdx = \dfrac{1}{2t}dt$

So, $I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)\dfrac{dt}{t}$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2} ∫ \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{{t}^{2}}\right)dt$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right) + c$

$⇒ I = \dfrac{1}{2}\left({\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{2x} - {\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{2x}\right) + C$

Now on comparing with $I = \dfrac{1}{\alpha}{\left(\dfrac{x}{e}\right)}^{\betax} - \dfrac{1}{\gamma}{\left(\dfrac{e}{x}\right)}^{\deltax} + C$, we get $\alpha = 2, \beta = 2, \gamma = 2, \delta = 2$

Hence, $\alpha + 2\beta + 3\gamma - 4\delta = 2 + 4 + 6 - 8 = 4$

Hence this is the required option.

Then the projection of $\overset{\to}{b}$ on the vector $\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}$ is:
38575.sol:
Given,

$\overset{\to}{a} = \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ , $\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} = 2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = 3$

Now using the formula ${\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = \left({\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\sin^{2}\theta + {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\cos^{2}\theta\right)$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}\left(\sin^{2}\theta + \cos^{2}\theta\right) = {\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} \cdot {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

We get,

$⇒ {\left|2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2} + {\left|3\right|}^{2} = {\left|\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right|}^{2}{\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}$

$⇒ {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} = \dfrac{5 + 9}{6} = \dfrac{14}{6} = \dfrac{7}{3}$

Now finding $\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right| = \sqrt{{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|}^{2} + {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2} - 2\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \sqrt{6 + \dfrac{7}{3} - 6} = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}}$

Now projection of $\overset{\to}{b}$ on $\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right|}$

$= \dfrac{\overset{\to}{b} \cdot \overset{\to}{a} - {\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|}^{2}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{3 - \dfrac{7}{3}}{\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{3}}}$

$= \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{21}}$

39097.subject: Physics
39097.text: A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacitance $C$. When it is half filled as show in figure with a dielectric constant $K = 5$, the percentage increase in the capacitance is _______.
39097.sol:
Initial capacitance of the air capacitor is given by:

$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$

When the capacitor is half-filled with a dielectric of thickness $d/2$, it can be considered as two capacitors connected in series.

Capacitance of the dielectric-filled part:

$C_1 = \dfrac{K \epsilon_0 A}{d/2} = \dfrac{2K \epsilon_0 A}{d} = 2KC$

Capacitance of the air-filled part:

$C_2 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d/2} = \dfrac{2 \epsilon_0 A}{d} = 2C$

The equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ of the series combination is:

$C_{eq} = \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2} = \dfrac{(2KC)(2C)}{2KC + 2C} = \dfrac{2K}{K+1} C$

Substituting $K = 5$:

$C_{eq} = \dfrac{2(5)}{5+1} C = \dfrac{10}{6} C = \dfrac{5}{3} C$

The increase in capacitance is:

$\Delta C = C_{eq} - C = \dfrac{5}{3} C - C = \dfrac{2}{3} C$

The percentage increase in capacitance is:

$\% \text{ increase} = \dfrac{\Delta C}{C} \times 100 = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 100 \approx 66.67\%$

Answer: $66.67$

39110.text: A parallel plate capacitor is filled equally (half) with two dielectrics of dielectric constant $\varepsilon_1$ and $\varepsilon_2$, as shown in figures. The distance between the plates is d and area of each plate is A. If capacitance in first configuration and second configuration are $C_1$ and $C_2$ respectively, then $\frac{C_1}{C_2}$ is :

Area of plate is $A$. then
$\begin{aligned}

\end{aligned}$
Let $\mathrm{C}_0=\frac{\varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{\mathrm{~d}}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{C}=2 \varepsilon_2 \mathrm{C}_0 \\ & \mathrm{C}^{\prime}=2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0
\end{aligned}$
$\mathrm{C} \& \mathrm{C}^{\prime}$ are in series
$\mathrm{C}_1=\frac{\mathrm{CC}^{\prime}}{\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{C}^{\prime}}=\frac{4 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0^2}{2 \mathrm{C}_0\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)}$
$=\frac{2 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0}{\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)}$
Here $\mathrm{C}=\frac{\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{~A}}{2 \mathrm{~d}}=\frac{\varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0}{2}$
$\mathrm{C}^{\prime}=\frac{\varepsilon_2 \mathrm{C}_0}{2}$
$\mathrm{C} \& \mathrm{C}^{\prime}$ are inparallel
$\mathrm{C}_2=\mathrm{C}^{\prime}+\mathrm{C}=\left(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2\right) \frac{\mathrm{C}_0}{2}$
Thus $\frac{\mathrm{C}_1}{\mathrm{C}_2}=\frac{2 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1 \mathrm{C}_0}{\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)} \times \frac{2}{\left(\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2\right) \mathrm{C}_0}$
$=\frac{4 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_1}{\left(\varepsilon_2+\varepsilon_1\right)^2}$

39148.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : Two metallic spheres are charged to the same potential. One of them is hollow and another is solid, and both have the same radii. Solid sphere will have lower charge than the hollow one.

Reason R : Capacitance of metallic spheres depend on the radii of spheres.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
39148.sol:
Potential of a conducting sphere is given by $V = \dfrac{KQ}{R}$

As in case of metallic sphere either solid or hollow, the charge will reside on the surface of the sphere. Since both spheres have same surface area, so they can hold equal charge.

$∴ {Q}_{1} = {Q}_{2}$

The capacitance of a metallic sphere depends only on its radius. It does not matter whether the sphere is hollow or solid.

Hence, A is false but R is true.

If the magnetic force acting on electron is $\overset{\to}{F} = 5e\overset{^}{k}N$, where $e$ is the charge of electron, then the value of ${B}_{0}$ is ____ $T$.
41462.sol:
Force acting on a charged particle under the magnetic field is given by, $\overset{\to}{F} = q\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$.

$⇒ 5e\overset{⏜}{k} = e\left(3\overset{⏜}{i} + 5\overset{⏜}{j}\right) \times \left({B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{i} + 2{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{j}\right)$

$⇒ 5e\overset{⏜}{k} = e\left(6{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{k} - 5{B}_{0}\overset{⏜}{k}\right)$

$⇒ {B}_{0} = 5T$

41519.text: A charge particle is moving in a uniform magnetic field $\left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right)T$. If it has an acceleration of $\left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j}\right)m{s}^{- 2}$, then the value of $\alpha$ will be
41519.sol:
The magnetic force on a moving charged particle is given by $\overset{\to}{F} = q\left(\overset{\to}{v} \times \overset{\to}{B}\right)$. Therefore, we know that the magnetic force is perpendicular to the magnetic field. Therefore, the resulting acceleration will also be perpendicular to the magnetic field. As the scalar product of two mutually perpendicular vectors is zero,

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{B} = 0 ⇒ \left(\alpha\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j}\right) \cdot \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 2\alpha - 12 = 0 ⇒ \alpha = 6$

41973.subject: Physics
41973.text: The diameter of an air bubble which was initially $2mm$, rises steadily through a solution of density $1750 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ at the rate of $0.35 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$. Coefficient of viscosity of the solution is ______ (Assume mass of the bubble to be negligible) (Answer in Poise to the nearest integer)
41973.sol:
As the bubble is rising steadily the net force acting on it will be zero.

(Because of density of air is negligible, so the value of $mg$ can be neglected)

So, the force of buoyancy $B$ is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid acting upward is equal to the viscous force acting downward, i.e., $B = F$.

$⇒ \dfrac{4\pi}{3}{R}^{3}ρg = 6\piηRv$

Putting $R = 1mm = {10}^{- 3}m$, $ρ = 1 . 75 \times {10}^{3}kg{m}^{- 3}$, g = 10m{s}^{- 2} and $v = 0 . 35 \times {10}^{- 2}m{s}^{- 1}$

$η = \dfrac{10}{9} = 1 \cdot 11$

In SI unit, $η = 11$ poise $\left(CGS\right)$.

42000.text: A large number of water drops, each of radius $r$, combine to have a drop of radius $R$. If the surface tension is $T$ and mechanical equivalent of heat is $J$, the rise in heat energy per unit volume will be:
42000.sol:
$n \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}$

$∴ {n}^{1 / 3}r = R$

$∴$ Total change in surface energy

$= \left(n\left(4\pi{r}^{2}\right) - 4\pi{R}^{2}\right)T$

$⇒ 4\piT\left(n{r}^{2} - {R}^{2}\right)$

$∴$ Heat energy

$= \dfrac{4\piT\left(n{r}^{2} - {R}^{2}\right)}{J \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}} = \dfrac{3T}{J}\left(\dfrac{n{r}^{2}}{{R}^{3}} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

Put $n{r}^{3} = {R}^{3}$

$∴ \dfrac{3T}{J}\left(\dfrac{1}{r} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

42025.text: A liquid of density $\rho$ is coming out of a hose pipe of radius a with horizontal speed $v$ and hits a mesh. $50 \%$ of the liquid passes through the mesh unaffected. $25 \%$ looses all of its momentum and $25 \%$ comes back with the same speed. 42025.sol:
Mass per unit time of the liquid = \rhoav Momentum per second carried by liquid $=\rho a v \times v$

Net force due to bounced back liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{1}=2 \times\left[\frac{1}{4} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}\right]$

Net force due to stopped liquid, $\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{4}$ pav $^{2}$ Total force,

$\mathrm{F}=\mathrm{F}_{1}+\mathrm{F}_{2}=\frac{1}{2} \rho \mathrm{av}^{2}+\frac{1}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2}=\frac{3}{4} \mathrm{pav}^{2}$

Net pressure $=\frac{3}{4} \rho v^{2}$

42417.text: An object is projected in the air with initial velocity $u$ at an angle $\theta$. The projectile motion is such that the horizontal range $R$, is maximum. Another object is projected in the air with a horizontal range half of the range of first object. The initial velocity remains same in both the case. The value of the angle of projection, at which the second object is projected, will be _____  degree.
42417.sol:
The maximum range is given by, ${R}_{max} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}sin2\left(45 °\right)}{g} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{g}$.

For the range to be half of the maximum range,

$\dfrac{{R}_{max}}{2} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}}{2g} = \dfrac{{u}^{2}sin2\theta}{g}$

$⇒ sin2\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 2\theta = 30 ° \text{or}2\theta = 150 °$

$⇒ \theta = 15 ° , 75 °$

Therefore, answer is $15\text{or}75$

42719.subject: Physics
42719.text: The potential energy of a particle of mass $4kg$ in motion along the $x$-axis is given by $U = 4\left(1 - cos4x\right)J$. The time period of the particle for small oscillation $\left(sin\theta ≃ \theta\right) \left(\dfrac{\pi}{K}\right)s$. The value of $K$ is _____ .
42719.sol:
Given here, potential energy, $U = 4\left(1 - cos4x\right)J$

Using the relation between conservative force and potential energy, $F = - \dfrac{d U}{d x}$.

We have, $F = - 4\left(+ sin4x\right)4 = - 16sin\left(4x\right)$

For small $\theta$, $sin\theta \approx \theta$.

Acceleration of particle is $a = - \dfrac{64x}{m} = \dfrac{- 64x}{4} = - 16x$

As the oscillations are simple harmonic in nature, so $a = - {\omega}^{2}x ⇒ {\omega}^{2} = 16 ⇒ \omega = 4rad{s}^{- 1}$

Now, time period of oscillation is$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Thus, the value of $K = 2$.

42774.sol:
Let the density of bob is $\sigma$ & density of liquid is $\dfrac{\sigma}{16}$ .
Now, Net downward force on bob = Weight - Buoyancy
$= \sigmaVg - \dfrac{\sigma}{16}Vg = \dfrac{15}{16}\sigmaVg$
Net effective gravitational acceleration $= \dfrac{\dfrac{15}{16}\sigmaVg}{\sigmaV} = \dfrac{15}{16}g$
Time period $\left(T\right) = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{{g}_{eff}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{\dfrac{15}{16}g}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{16}{15}\dfrac{l}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{16}{15}} ∙ \left(2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}\right) = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{15}}T$
$= 4T\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{15}}$

43340.text: A rectangular solid box of length $0.3m$ is held horizontally, with one of its sides on the edge of a platform of height $5m$ . When released, it slips off the table in a very short time $τ = 0.01s$ , remaining essentially horizontal. The angle by which it would rotate when it hits the ground will be (in radians) close to:
43340.sol:
Angular impulse = change in angular momentum
$τ\Deltat = \DeltaL$
$mg\dfrac{l}{2} \times 0.01 = \dfrac{m{l}^{2}}{3}\omega$
$\omega = \dfrac{3g \times 0.01}{2l} = \dfrac{3 \times 10 \times 0.01}{2 \times 0.3} = 0.5rad / sec$
Time taken by rod to hit the ground = $\sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times 5}{10}} = 1s$
Angle rotated by rod = $\omegat = 0.5 \times 1 = 0.5rad$

43705.subject: Physics
43705.text: According to law of equipartition of energy the molar specific heat of a diatomic gas at constant volume where the molecule has one additional vibrational mode is :-
43705.sol:
A diatomic gas has 5 degrees of freedom apart from vibrational degree of freedom. For each additional vibrational mode, degree of freedom is increased by $2$. So new degree of freedom,

$f = 5 + 2 = 7$

Therefore, we require molar specific heat capacity at constant volume, which is given by

${C}_{v} = \dfrac{f}{2}R = \dfrac{7}{2}R$

44377.subject: Physics
44377.text: The speed of a longitudinal wave in a metallic bar is $400 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the density and Young's modulus of the bar material are increased by $0.5 \%$ and $1 \%$, respectively then the speed of the wave is changed approximately to $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
44377.sol:
The speed of a longitudinal wave in a solid is given by $v = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}$ where $Y$ is Young's modulus and $\rho$ is density.
Initial condition: $v_0 = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}} = 400$ m/s
After changes: $\rho' = 1.005\rho$ (0.5% increase) and $Y' = 1.01Y$ (1% increase)
New speed: $v' = \sqrt{\frac{Y'}{\rho'}} = \sqrt{\frac{1.01Y}{1.005\rho}} = \sqrt{\frac{1.01}{1.005}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}$
$\frac{v'}{v_0} = \sqrt{\frac{1.01}{1.005}} = \sqrt{1.00498...} \approx 1.00249$
$v' = 400 \times 1.00249 \approx 401$ m/s

Meiosis I is reductional and Meisois II is equational

46592.text: A disc of moment of inertia $2 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2$ revolving with $8 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ is placed on another disc of moment of inertia $4 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2$ revolving $4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$. What is the angular frequency of composite disc?
46592.sol:
Given that, moment of inertia of discs,
$\mathrm{I}_1=2 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2, \mathrm{I}_2=4 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2$
Angular velocity of discs, $\omega_1=8 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$, $\omega_2=4 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
From angular momentum conservation principle,
$\mathrm{I}_1 \omega_1+\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2=\left(\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2\right) \omega$
or $\quad 2 \times 8+4 \times 4=(2+4) \omega$
or $\quad \omega=\frac{16+16}{6}=\frac{32}{6}=\frac{16}{3} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$

46712.text: An engine moving towards a wall with a velocity $50 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ emits a note of 1.2 kHz . Speed of sound in air is $350 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The frequency of the note after reflection from the wall as heard by the driver of the engine is
46712.sol:
The reflected sound appears to propagate in a direction opposite to that of moving engine. Thus, the source and the observer can be presumed to approach each other with same velocity.
$v^{\prime}=\frac{v\left(v+v_o\right)}{\left(v-v_s\right)}$
$=v\left(\frac{v+v_s}{v-v_s}\right) \quad\left(\because v_o=v_s\right)$
$\Rightarrow \quad v^{\prime}=1.2\left(\frac{350+50}{350-50}\right)$
$=\frac{1.2 \times 400}{300}$
$=1.6 \mathrm{kHz}$

48065.text: Which among the following has highest $\mathrm{pH}$ ?
48065.sol:
For acidic medium, we know that $\mathrm{pH}$ values range is between $0-6.9$, for neutral it is 7 and for bases it is $7.1-14$. So, $\mathrm{HCl}$ is acidic and $\mathrm{NaOH}$ is basic. Thus, we can straight forward infer that $\mathrm{NaOH}$ has a higher $\mathrm{pH}$ value.
Now, 1 mole of sodium hydroxide produces 1 mole of $\mathrm{Na}^{+}$and 1 mole of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ions. This means that the concentration of the hydroxide ions will be equal to $\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]=[\mathrm{NaOH}]=1 \mathrm{M}$
For case $\mathrm{A}$,

$\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{pOH}=-\log \left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]=-\log [$1]=0 \\
& \therefore \quad $\mathrm{pH}=$14-$\mathrm{pOH}=$14-0=14 \\
& $\text{$ For case }B $\text{, }$\\
& {$\left[\mathrm{OH}^{-}\right]=[\mathrm{NaOH}]=$0.1 $\mathrm{M}$} \\
& $\text{ pOH }=-\log [$0.1]=1 \\
& \therefore \quad $\mathrm{pH}=$14-1=13 \\
&
\end{aligned}

So, pH$ of 1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{NaOH}$ is highest among the given solution.

Given,
$f(x)=\frac{x}{3}+\frac{3}{x}$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{3}{x^{2}}
$Since, function is decreasing
$\begin{array}{ll}
\text{ i.e., } & f^{\prime}(x) < 0 \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{3}-\frac{3}{x^{2}} < 0 \\
\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{3} < \frac{3}{x^{2}} \\
\Rightarrow & x^{2} < 9 \\
\Rightarrow & x \in(-3,3)
\end{array}$
which is the required interval in which function $f(x)$ decreases.

54429.text: The kinetic energy $k$ of a particle moving along a circle of radius $R$ depends on the distance covered. It is given as $\mathrm{KE}=a s^2$, where $a$ is a constant. The force acting on the particle is
54429.sol:
In non-uniform circular motion two forces will work on a particle $F_c$ and $F_t$.
So, the net force $F_{\text{Net }}=\sqrt{F_c^2+F_t^2}$...(i)
Centripetal force $F_c=\frac{m v^2}{R}=\frac{2 a s^2}{R}$...(ii)
[given $\frac{1}{2} m v^2=a s^2$ given]
Again from $\frac{1}{2} m v^2=a s^2\Rightarrow \quad v^2=\frac{2 a s^2}{m} \Rightarrow \quad v=s \sqrt{\frac{2 a}{m}}$
Tangential acceleration $a_t=\frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{d v}{d s} \cdot \frac{d s}{d t}\Rightarrow \quad a_t=\frac{d}{d s}\left[s \sqrt{\frac{2 a}{m}}\right] \cdot va_t=v \sqrt{\frac{2 a}{m}}=s \sqrt{\frac{2 a}{m}} \sqrt{\frac{2 a}{m}}=\frac{2 a s}{m}$
and $\quad F_t=m a_t=2 a s$...(iii)
Now, on substituting value of $F_c$ and $F_t$ in Eq. (i), we get
$\therefore F_{\text{Net }}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{2 a s^2}{R}\right)^2+(2 a s)^2}=2 a s\left[1+\frac{s^2}{R^2}\right]^{1 / 2}$

55473.subject: Chemistry
55473.text: What is the total number of -OH groups present in a nucleoside involved in formation of DNA?
55473.sol:
A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base and a pentose sugar. In DNA, the pentose is 2′-deoxyribose, which differs from ribose by the absence of a hydroxyl group at the 2′ position.

The hydroxyl groups in 2′-deoxyribose are as follows: the 1′ carbon is bonded to the nitrogenous base and lacks a free $\mathrm{-OH}$, the 2′ carbon has a hydrogen atom ($\mathrm{-H}$) instead of $\mathrm{-OH}$, the 3′ carbon has a hydroxyl group, the 4′ carbon is part of the ring structure without a free $\mathrm{-OH}$, and the 5′ carbon has a hydroxyl group.

Thus, a 2′-deoxyribonucleoside has two hydroxyl groups: one at the 3′ position and one at the 5′ position.

$\boxed{2}$

57606.subject: Chemistry
57606.text: The reaction of aryl halide with sodium metal in dry ether to give biphenyl is known as
57606.sol:
The reaction of aryl halides with sodium metal in dry ether to form biphenyl constitutes the Fittig reaction. This transformation produces biaryl compounds through the general reaction $\mathrm{Ar-X + 2Na + X-Ar \rightarrow Ar-Ar + 2NaX}$.

The Swartz reaction employs metallic fluorides to synthesize alkyl fluorides and does not involve aryl halides or biphenyl formation. The Wurtz reaction couples two alkyl halides to form alkanes: $\mathrm{R-X + 2Na + X-R \rightarrow R-R + 2NaX}$.

Although the Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves aryl halides, it requires an alkyl halide co-reactant and produces alkylarenes rather than biaryls.

Since the transformation specifically couples two aryl halide molecules to form a biaryl compound, it corresponds exclusively to the Fittig reaction.

58874.subject: Chemistry
58874.text: Calculate the total number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids formed in 0.6 mol of a compound if it forms hcp structure.
58874.sol:
Number of atoms in 0.6 mol: Since 1 mol contains $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ atoms, the total number is $0.6 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.6132 \times 10^{23}$.

Voids in hcp structure: Octahedral voids equal the number of atoms, giving $3.6132 \times 10^{23}$.
Tetrahedral voids are twice the number of atoms, yielding $2 \times 3.6132 \times 10^{23} = 7.2264 \times 10^{23}$.

Total voids: Summing both gives $3.6132 \times 10^{23} + 7.2264 \times 10^{23} = 10.8396 \times 10^{23}$.
Expressed with three significant figures, this is $1.084 \times 10^{24}$.

This matches option C.

59863.subject: Chemistry
59863.text: Identify the law for the statement "Overall the enthalpy change for a reaction is equal to sum of enthalpy changes of individual steps in the reaction"
59863.sol:
Hess's law of constant heat summation states that the total enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is independent of the path by which the reaction occurs.

If a reaction takes place in several steps, the overall enthalpy change is equal to the sum of the enthalpy changes of the individual steps. This is because enthalpy is a state function, meaning it depends only on the initial and final states of the system, not on the path taken.

Answer: Hess's law

60279.sol:
The approximation for $\cos(59^{}^{\circ} 30')$ uses linear approximation with $f(x) = \cos x$, giving $f(x_0 + \Delta x) \approx f(x_0) + f'(x_0)\Delta x$.

With $x_0 = 60^{}^{\circ}$ and $\Delta x = -30' = -0.5^{}^{\circ}$, convert $\Delta x$ to radians using $1^{}^{\circ} = 0.0175^\text{c}$, so $\Delta x = -0.5 \times 0.0175 = -0.00875^\text{c}$.

Given $\cos(60^{}^{\circ}) = 0.5$ and $\sin(60^{}^{\circ}) = 0.8660$, then $f'(x_0) = -\sin(60^{}^{\circ}) = -0.8660$.

Substitute into the approximation: $\cos(59^{}^{\circ} 30') \approx 0.5 + (-0.8660)(-0.00875) = 0.5 + 0.0075775 = 0.5075775$.

Rounded to four decimal places, this yields $0.5076$, matching option A.

64421.text: The line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{-1}=\frac{\mathrm{z}}{1}$ intersects the XY plane and the YZ plane at points $A$ and $B$ respectively. The equation of line through the points $A$ and $B$ is
64421.sol:
Find the line through A and B, where A is the intersection of the line $\frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y+2}{-1}=\frac{z}{1}$ with the XY plane ($z=0$), and B is its intersection with the YZ plane ($x=0$).

Set z=0 and $\frac{z}{1}=0$ in the parametric ratio, yielding $\frac{x-1}{2}=0 and \frac{y+2}{-1}=0$. Thus, $x=1$, $y=-2$, and $A$ is $(1, -2, 0)$.

Set $x=0$ and denote $\frac{0-1}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}$. From $\frac{y+2}{-1} = -\frac{1}{2}$, cross-multiplying gives $y+2 = \frac{1}{2}$, so $y = -\frac{3}{2}$. Similarly, $\frac{z}{1} = -\frac{1}{2}$, so $z = -\frac{1}{2}$, and $B$ is $\left(0, -\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)$.

The direction vector from A to B is $\vec{b} - \vec{a} = (0-1)\hat{i} + \left(-\frac{3}{2} + 2\right)\hat{j} + \left(-\frac{1}{2} - 0\right)\hat{k} = -\hat{i} + \frac{1}{2}\hat{j} - \frac{1}{2}\hat{k}$.

Using point A and this direction, the vector equation is $\left[\vec{r} - (\hat{i} - 2\hat{j})\right] \times \left(-\hat{i} + \frac{1}{2}\hat{j} - \frac{1}{2}\hat{k}\right) = \overline{0}$, matching option A.

65096.text: Let $\bar{a}, \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ be three coplanar unit vectors. A unit vector $\bar{d}$ is perpendicular to them. If $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times (\bar{c} \times \bar{d}) = \dfrac{3}{26}\hat{i} - \dfrac{2}{13}\hat{j} + \dfrac{6}{13}\hat{k}$ and the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is $30^{}^{\circ}$, then $\bar{c}$ is equal to...
65096.sol:
Using the vector quadruple product expansion:

$(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times (\bar{c} \times \bar{d}) = [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{d}]\bar{c} - [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]\bar{d}$

Since $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are coplanar, their scalar triple product $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] = 0$.

Thus, the expression simplifies to $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{d}]\bar{c}$.

The scalar triple product is $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{d}] = (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{d}$.

Since $\bar{d}$ is perpendicular to the coplanar vectors $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$, the vector $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ is parallel to $\bar{d}$.

The magnitude of $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ is given by $|\bar{a}| |\bar{b}| \sin 30^{}^{\circ} = 1 \times 1 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $\bar{d}$ is a unit vector, $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{d} = \pm |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}| |\bar{d}| = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Therefore, $\pm \dfrac{1}{2} \bar{c} = \dfrac{3}{26}\hat{i} - \dfrac{2}{13}\hat{j} + \dfrac{6}{13}\hat{k}$.

Multiplying by $\pm 2$ yields:

$\bar{c} = \pm \left( \dfrac{3}{13}\hat{i} - \dfrac{4}{13}\hat{j} + \dfrac{12}{13}\hat{k} \right)$

Taking the positive sign gives the matching option.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{13}$\hat{i} - $\dfrac{4}{13}$\hat{j} + $\dfrac{12}{13}$\hat{k}$$

65567.text: Determine the frequency for which a $10\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor has a reactance of $2 \times 10^{-3}\,\Omega$.
65567.sol:
The capacitive reactance is given by the formula:

$X_C = \dfrac{1}{2\pi f C}$

Rearranging for frequency $f$:

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi X_C C}$

Substituting the given values $X_C = 2 \times 10^{-3} \, \Omega$ and $C = 10 \, \mu\text{F} = 10 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{F}$:

$f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi \times (2 \times 10^{-3}) \times (10 \times 10^{-6})}$

$f = \dfrac{1}{4\pi \times 10^{-8}}$

$f = \dfrac{10^8}{4\pi}$

$f = \dfrac{100 \times 10^6}{4\pi}$

$f = \dfrac{25}{\pi} \times 10^6 \, \text{Hz}$

$f = \dfrac{25}{\pi} \, \text{MHz}$

66060.subject: Physics
66060.text: The capacity of air filled parallel plate capacitor is $\mathrm{C}_0$. One-half of the space between the plates is filled with a dielectric constant ' $K$ ' as shown in figure. The new capacity becomes $C_n$. The ratio $C_n$ to $C_0$ is
66060.sol:
The capacitance of the air-filled parallel plate capacitor is $C_0 = \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$.

When one-half of the space is filled with dielectric constant $K$ while the other half remains air-filled, the configuration becomes equivalent to two parallel capacitors. The dielectric-filled portion has capacitance $C_1 = \frac{K \epsilon_0 (A/2)}{d} = \frac{K}{2} C_0$, and the air-filled portion has $C_2 = \frac{\epsilon_0 (A/2)}{d} = \frac{1}{2} C_0$.

The total new capacitance is $C_n = C_1 + C_2 = \frac{K}{2} C_0 + \frac{1}{2} C_0 = C_0 \left(\frac{K+1}{2}\right).

The ratio \frac{C_n}{C_0} = \frac{K+1}{2}.

Final answer: \boxed{\frac{K+1}{2}}$

67051.text: Three point charges $+Q+2 Q$ and $q$ are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle. The value of charge q in terms of Q , so that electrical potential energy of the system is zero, is given by
67051.sol:
For the system's electrical potential energy to be zero, the total potential energy must satisfy $U_{\text{total}} = 0$. The potential energy between two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ separated by distance $a$ is $\frac{k q_1 q_2}{a}$, where $k = \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$.

The three pairs contribute:
$U_{12} = \frac{k(Q)(2Q)}{a} = \frac{2kQ^2}{a}$
$U_{13} = \frac{kQq}{a}$
$U_{23} = \frac{k(2Q)q}{a} = \frac{2kQq}{a}$

Summing these gives $U_{\text{total}} = \frac{k}{a}(2Q^2 + 3Qq)$. Setting this equal to zero and solving yields $2Q^2 + 3Qq = 0$, so $q = -\frac{2}{3}Q$.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

67419.text: The r.m.s. speed of gas molecules at 800 K will be
options: four times the value at 200 K
67419.sol:
The root mean square speed is given by $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}$, showing $v_{\text{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}$.

For temperatures $T_1 = 800\text{ K}$ and $T_2 = 200\text{ K}$, the ratio becomes $\frac{v_1}{v_2} = \sqrt{\frac{800}{200}} = \sqrt{4} = 2$.

The r.m.s. speed at 800 K is therefore twice that at 200 K.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{B}}$

\therefore $\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{H}}$&=$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{o}}$\\

68009.text: A vector $\vec{A}$ when added to the sum of the vectors $(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})$ and $(-2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})$ gives a unit vector along Y axis. The magnitude of vector $\vec{A}$ is
68009.sol:
Let the given vectors be $\vec{V}_1 = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{V}_2 = -2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$.

The sum of these vectors is $\vec{V}_1 + \vec{V}_2 = -\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

According to the given condition, $\vec{A} + (\vec{V}_1 + \vec{V}_2) = \hat{j}$.

Substituting the sum, we get $\vec{A} + (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = \hat{j}$.

$\vec{A} = \hat{j} - (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}$.

The magnitude of vector $\vec{A}$ is $|\vec{A}| = \sqrt{1^2 + 2^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{6}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{6}$

69347.text:
A thin circular ring of mass ' $\mathrm{M}^{\prime}$ and radius ' $\mathrm{R}^{\prime}$ is rotating about a transverse axis
passing through its centre with constant angular velocity ' $\omega$ '. Two objects each of
mass 'm' are attached gently to the opposite ends of a diameter of the ring. What is the new angular velocity?
69347.sol:
Initial angular momentum of the ring $\quad=I \omega=M R^{2} \omega$
If the new angular velocity is $\omega^{\prime}$ then the final angular momentum $=I^{\prime} \omega^{\prime}$ where $I^{\prime}=M R^{2}+2 m R^{2}=(M+2 m) R^{2}$.
By law of conservation of momentum
$\begin{array}{c}
\mathrm{I}^{\prime} \omega^{\prime}=\mathrm{I} \omega \\
(\mathrm{M}+2 \mathrm{ m}) \mathrm{R}^{2} \omega^{\prime} \\
\therefore \omega^{\prime}=\frac{\mathrm{M} \omega}{\mathrm{M}+2 \mathrm{ m}}
\end{array}=\mathrm{MR}^{2} \omega$

69473.subject: Physics
69473.text: In a common emitter transistor amplifier, the output voltage and input voltage have a phase difference of
69473.sol:
Common Emitter Amplifier Phase Shift

In a common emitter configuration, the input signal is applied between base and emitter, with output taken across collector and emitter. Increasing base voltage raises base current $I_B$, which in turn increases collector current $I_C$ according to $I_C = \beta I_B$.

The output voltage follows $V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C R_C$. As $I_C$ rises, the voltage drop $I_C R_C$ increases, causing $V_{CE}$ to decrease. This inverse relationship creates a phase shift of $\pi$ radians between input and output voltages.

The phase difference is $\pi^c$.

Answer: D

70889.subject: Biology
70889.text: An additional apoplastic route that allows direct access to xylem is along the secondary roots because they ______.
options: are made up of non-living cells
70889.sol:
Secondary roots (lateral roots) originate from the pericycle, which is a layer of cells located just inside the endodermis.

As these secondary roots grow outward, they break through the endodermis and its Casparian strip.

This disruption creates a gap in the endodermal barrier, providing an additional apoplastic route that allows water and solutes direct access to the xylem, bypassing the Casparian strip.

Answer: develop from pericycle

70930.subject: Biology
70930.text: The introduction of African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) for aquaculture purposes has proved harmful to endemic catfish varieties mainly because African catfish ____.
70930.sol:
When an exotic or alien species is introduced into a new geographical area, it often becomes invasive and spreads rapidly, causing a decline in the population of indigenous species.

This rapid spread and dominance occur primarily because the invaded ecosystem lacks the natural predators that would otherwise keep the exotic species' population under control.

The African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) was introduced illegally for aquaculture purposes and became a major threat to the endemic catfish varieties in Indian rivers because it has no local predators, allowing it to multiply unchecked and outcompete native species for resources.

Answer: has no local predators.

70980.subject: Biology
70980.text: Which chemical element is found in high amounts in nuclein?
70980.sol:
Nuclein was the term originally coined by Friedrich Miescher for the substance he discovered in the nuclei of white blood cells, which is now known as nucleic acid (DNA and RNA).

Nucleic acids are composed of nucleotides, which consist of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group. Because of the phosphate backbone, nuclein contains a high amount of phosphorus.

Miescher specifically noted that nuclein was rich in phosphorus and lacked sulphur, which helped distinguish it from proteins.

Answer: Phosphorus

71275.subject: Biology
71275.text:
Identify the correct features of the genetic code.
i. It is a triplet code.
ii. It shows distinct polarity.
iii. It is overlapping.
iv. The genetic code was deciphered by Watson and Crick.
71275.sol:
The genetic code is a triplet code, meaning three nitrogenous bases code for one amino acid.

It has a distinct polarity and is always read in the $5' \rightarrow 3'$ direction on the mRNA.

The genetic code is non-overlapping, meaning each base is part of only one codon.

The genetic code was deciphered by Marshall Nirenberg, Heinrich Matthaei, and Har Gobind Khorana, not by Watson and Crick. Watson and Crick proposed the double-helical structure of DNA.

Thus, statements (i) and (ii) are correct.

Answer: Statement (i) and Statement (ii) are correct.

71762.subject: Chemistry
71762.text: How long (in minutes) must a $2\ \text{A}$ current be passed through $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution to deposit $5.4\ \text{g Ag}$? [Molar mass of Ag $= 108\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$]
71762.sol:
According to Faraday's first law of electrolysis:

$m = \dfrac{E \times I \times t}{96500}$

Here, $m = 5.4\ \text{g}$, $I = 2\ \text{A}$, and equivalent weight of Ag, $E = \dfrac{108}{1} = 108\ \text{g eq}^{-1}$.

Substituting the values:

$5.4 = \dfrac{108 \times 2 \times t}{96500}$

$t = \dfrac{5.4 \times 96500}{108 \times 2}$

$t = 2412.5\ \text{s}$

Converting time into minutes:

$t = \dfrac{2412.5}{60}\ \text\min \approx 40.2\ \text\min$

Answer: $40.2\ \text\min$.

72079.text:
In the LCR series circuit, an alternating e.m.f. $e$ and current $i$ are given by the equation $e = 100\sin(100t)\,V$ and $i = 100\sin\left(100t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)mA$.
The average power dissipated in the circuit will be
$\{\sin(\pi/3) = 3^{0.5}/2,\ \cos(\pi/3) = 1/2\}$
72079.sol:
The given equations for alternating e.m.f. and current are:

$e = 100\sin(100t)$ V

$i = 100\sin \left(100t + \dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) mA

From the equations, the peak voltage $ E_0 = 100$ V, the peak current $I_0 = 100$ mA $= 0.1$ A, and the phase difference $\phi = $\dfrac{\pi}{3}.

The average power dissipated in an AC circuit is given by:

$ P_{avg} = E_{rms} I_{rms} \cos\phi = $\dfrac{E_0 I_0}{2} \cos\phi

Substituting the given values:

$ P_{avg} = $\dfrac{100 \times 0.1}{2} \cos \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)

$ P_{avg} = $\dfrac{10}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} =2.5$ W

Answer: $2.5$ W

72213.subject: Physics
72213.text: A charge Q is distributed over the two concentric hollow spheres of radii $r$ and $R$ (R > r$) such the surface densities are equal. The potential at the common centre is {K = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0}$, $\epsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space}
72213.sol:
Let $q_1$ and $q_2$ be the charges on the inner and outer spheres respectively.

Given $q_1 + q_2 = Q$

Since the surface charge densities are equal, $\sigma_1 = \sigma_2 = \sigma$

$\dfrac{q_1}{4\pi r^2} = \dfrac{q_2}{4\pi R^2} = \sigma$

$q_1 = \sigma 4\pi r^2$ and $q_2 = \sigma 4\pi R^2$

Total charge $Q = \sigma 4\pi (r^2 + R^2) \Rightarrow \sigma = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi (r^2 + R^2)}$

The potential at the common centre is the sum of the potentials due to both spheres:

$V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q_1}{r} + \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{q_2}{R}$

$V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{\sigma 4\pi r^2}{r} + \dfrac{\sigma 4\pi R^2}{R} \right)

$V = $\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0} ($ r + R)$

Substituting the value of \sigma:

$ V = $\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0 (r^2 + R^2)} ($ r + R)$

Given $K = $\dfrac{Q}{4\pi\epsilon_0}, we get:

$ V = $\dfrac{K(r+R)}{R^2+r²}

Answer: \dfrac{K(r+R)}{(R²+r²)}$

72368.subject: Physics
72368.text: Which of the following is true for a p-type semiconductor?
options: The impurity level lies just above the valence band.
The impurity level is just below the conduction band.
The impurity level is near the conduction band.
72368.sol:
In a p-type semiconductor, trivalent impurity atoms (such as boron, aluminum, or gallium) are added to an intrinsic semiconductor.

These impurity atoms create an acceptor energy level which lies just above the valence band.

Electrons from the valence band can easily transition to this acceptor level at room temperature, leaving behind holes in the valence band. Thus, holes become the majority charge carriers.

Therefore, the impurity level lies just above the valence band.

Answer: The impurity level lies just above the valence band.

73798.subject: General Ability
73798.text: A floating body is in stable state. Which one of the following is correct?
options: The centre of gravity of the body is above its centre of buoyancy.
The centre of gravity of the body is below its centre of buoyancy.
The centre of gravity of the body coincides with its centre of buoyancy.
The centre of gravity of the body is below the metacentre.
73798.sol:
For a floating body, the condition for equilibrium and stability depends on the relative positions of its centre of gravity and its metacentre.

When a floating body is given a small angular displacement, its centre of buoyancy shifts. The point where the vertical line passing through the new centre of buoyancy intersects the original vertical axis is known as the metacentre.

For the body to be in a stable state, a restoring couple must act on it to bring it back to its original vertical position. This restoring couple is only produced if the metacentre lies above the centre of gravity.

Thus, for stable equilibrium of a floating body, its centre of gravity must be below the metacentre.

73855.subject: General Ability
73855.text: If the speed of light in carbon disulfide and vacuum is $X$ and $Y$ respectively, then
73855.sol:
The speed of light in a vacuum is the maximum speed at which light can travel.

When light enters any material medium, its speed decreases due to the optical density of the medium.

The refractive index of a medium is given by $\mu = \dfrac{Y}{X}$, where $Y$ is the speed of light in vacuum and $X$ is the speed of light in the medium.

Since the refractive index of carbon disulfide is greater than $1$ (\mu > 1$), we have \dfrac{Y}{X} > 1$.

This implies $X < Y$.

Answer: $X < Y$

75260.text:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Hypocenter is the point on the surface of the Earth, nearest to the focus.
2. Velocity of earthquake waves is higher in denser materials.
3. $P$ waves move faster and are the first to arrive at the surface of the Earth.
Select the correct answer using the code given below :
75260.sol:
The subsurface location (focus) at which the energy of an earthquake is released is known as hypocentre. Earthquakes generally occur at depths less than about 30 km.
P waves are the fastest body waves and arrive at stations before the S waves, or secondary waves. Their velocity in the crust varies between 5.0 and $7.0 \mathrm{ km} / \mathrm{s}$. Seismic waves move more slowly through a liquid than a solid. Molten areas within the Earth slow down $P$ waves and stop $S$ waves because their shearing motion cannot be transmitted through a liquid.

76355.subject: Mathematics
76355.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 5}$:
Statement-I: $f(x)$ is decreasing on the intervals $x < 5$ and $x > 5$.
Statement-II: $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x \neq 5$.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct
Statement-I is not correct but Statement-II is correct
76355.sol:
Given the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 5}$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:
$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}(x - 5)^{-1} = -1(x - 5)^{-2} = -\dfrac{1}{(x - 5)^2}$

For all $x eq 5$, $(x - 5)^2 > 0$, which implies $f'(x) < 0$.

Since $f'(x) < 0$ for all $x eq 5$, the function $f(x)$ is strictly decreasing on the interval $(-\infty, 5)$ and strictly decreasing on the interval $(5, \infty)$.

Therefore, Statement-I is correct.

Statement-II claims that $f'(x) > 0$ for all $x eq 5$, which contradicts our finding that $f'(x) < 0$. Thus, Statement-II is not correct.

Hence, Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct.

Answer: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is not correct

76405.text: What is the minimum value of $a^2 x+b^2 y$ where $x y=c^2$ ?

76809.subject: Mathematics
76809.text:
Passage: Let $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin x+b\cos x}{(a+b)(\sin x+\cos x)}\,dx=k$.

Question: What is $\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\cos x+b\sin x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$ equal to ?
76809.sol:
Given $\displaystyle k = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin x+b\cos x}{(a+b)(\sin x+\cos x)}\,dx$

Multiplying both sides by $(a+b)$:

$\displaystyle k(a+b) = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin x+b\cos x}{\sin x+\cos x}\,dx$

Using the definite integral property $\displaystyle \int_0^a f(x)\,dx = \int_0^a f(a-x)\,dx$, replacing $x$ with $\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x$:

$\displaystyle k(a+b) = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+b\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)+\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}\,dx$

$\displaystyle k(a+b) = \int_0^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}\dfrac{a\cos x+b\sin x}{\cos x+\sin x}\,dx$

This matches the required integral. Thus, the value is $k(a+b)$.

Answer: $k(a+b)$

If $A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 & a \\ 0 & 1\end{array}\right]$ where $a \in \mathbb{N}$, then what is $A^{100}-A^{50}-2 A^{25}$ equal to?

78388.subject: Mathematics
78388.text: If the harmonic mean of 60 and $x$ is 48 , then what is the value of $x$ ?
78388.sol:
If the Harmonic mean of 60 and $x$ is 48 , then
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{2}{48}=\frac{1}{60}+\frac{1}{x} \\
& \frac{1}{x}=\frac{2}{48}-\frac{1}{60}=\frac{1}{12}\left[\frac{2}{4}-\frac{1}{5}\right] \\
& \frac{1}{x}=\frac{1}{12} \times \frac{10-4}{20}=\frac{6}{12 \times 20} \\
& \therefore x=40
\end{aligned}$

79244.subject: Mathematics
79244.text:
Consider the following statements in respect of a vector $\vec{d} = (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c}$:
I. $\vec{d}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$.
II. $\vec{d}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
79244.sol:
Given $\vec{d} = (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c}$

Using the vector triple product expansion:

$\vec{d} = (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c})\vec{a}$

This shows that $\vec{d}$ is expressed as a linear combination of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. Thus, $\vec{d}$ lies in the plane containing $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, making it coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. Statement I is correct.

By the definition of the cross product, the vector resulting from the cross product of two vectors is perpendicular to both of them. Since $\vec{d}$ is the cross product of $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ and $\vec{c}$, it must be perpendicular to both $(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})$ and $\vec{c}$.

Therefore, $\vec{d} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$, which means $\vec{d}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$. Statement II is correct.

Both statements I and II are correct.

Answer: Both I and II

79670.subject: Botany
79670.text: Which one of the following statements about viruses is correct?
options: viruses possess their own metabolic system
all viruses contain both RNA and DNA
nucleic acid of viruses is known as capsid
79670.sol:
Viruses consist of a protein coat known as capsid which encloses a single type of nucleic acid, either RNA or DNA. They do not have enzymes for protein synthesis. They require living host cell for multiplication, while they take over the machinery of the host cell. Thus, viruses are obligatory intercellular parasites.
Related Theory
Viruses can infect all cellular life forms, but each cellular species can be infected by own limited specific range of viruses. Most viruses that harm animals can not harm humans.

79757.subject: Botany
79757.text: Which of the following types of plastid does not contain stored food material?
79757.sol:
Chromoplasts are yellow or reddish in colour because of the presence of carotenoid pigments. They do not contain stored food material. Chromoplast are formed either from leucoplast or chloroplast.
Related Theory
Chromoplasts are the plastids which are yellow or reddish in colour because of the presence of fat-soluble carotenoid pigments. Chlorophylls are absent in these plastids. Depending upon the dominant pigments present in plastids, chromoplasts are further classified into rhodoplasts that are rich in red pigment; phaeoplasts and xanthoplasts that contain yellow pigments. Chromoplasts are formed either from leucoplasts or chloroplasts. Change of colour from green to reddish during the ripening of many fruits, for example, Tomato and Chilli, is due to transformation of chloroplasts to chromoplasts. The chromoplasts also provide colour to many fruits and flowers.

80219.text: Which pigment absorbs the red and far-red light?

Phytochrome occurs in 2 forms, i.e., $\mathrm{P}_r$ and $\mathrm{P}_{f r}$ (i.e., red light and far-red light absorbing forms) and these 2 forms are interconvertible. Cytochromes are electron transferring proteins. They contain iron porphyrin or copper porphyrin as prosthetic groups. Chlorophyll is the fundamental green pigment of photosynthesis. It is localized on the chloroplasts. Carotenoids are lipid compounds and they are yellow, orange, purple etc. in colour.

82308.text: A body of mass $\left(4m\right)$ is lying in $x$ - $y$ plane at rest. It suddenly explodes into three pieces. Two pieces, each of mass $\left(m\right)$ move perpendicular to each other with equal speeds $\left(υ\right) .$ The total kinetic energy generated due to explosion is:
82308.sol:
The total momentum of the system will be conserved before and after explosion.

Then, ${p}_{i} = {p}_{f}$
$O = mv\overset{^}{i} + mv\overset{^}{j} + 2m\overset{\to}{v}$
$\overset{\to}{v} = - \dfrac{v}{2}\overset{^}{i} - \dfrac{v}{2}\overset{^}{j}$

83243.subject: Physics
83243.text: Two radioactive materials $X_1$ and $X_2$ have decay constants $5 \lambda$ and $\lambda$ respectively. If initially they have the same number of nuclei, then the ratio of the number of nuclei of $X_1$ to that of $X_2$ will be $\frac{1}{e}$ after a time
83243.sol:
If $N$ is the number of radioactive nuclei present at some instant, then
$N=N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$
The constant $N_0$ represents the number of radioactive nuclei at $t=0$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{N_1}{N_2}=\frac{e^{-\lambda_1 t}}{e^{-\lambda_2 t}} \\
& \frac{N_1}{N_2}=\frac{e^{-5 \lambda t}}{e^{-\lambda t}}=e^{-4 \lambda t} \\
& \frac{N_1}{N_2}=\frac{1}{e}
\end{aligned}$
but $\frac{N_1}{N_2}=\frac{1}{e}$ (as provided)
Therefore, $\frac{1}{e}=\frac{1}{e^{4 \lambda t}}$ or $4 \lambda t=1
or t=\frac{1}{4 \lambda}$

83266.subject: Physics
83266.text: For a simple pendulum, having time period $T$, the variation of kinetic energy (K.E.) with time (t) is represented by :
83266.sol:
The displacement of a simple pendulum executing simple harmonic motion is given by $x = A \sin(\omega t + \phi)$.

The velocity of the pendulum is $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = A \omega \cos(\omega t + \phi)$.

The kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m A^2 \omega^2 \cos^2(\omega t + \phi)$.

Since kinetic energy is proportional to the square of velocity, it can never be negative. This eliminates the graphs that show negative values.

Also, the kinetic energy of a pendulum is not constant, which eliminates the constant graph.

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos^2 \theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos(2\theta)}{2}$, we get:

$K = \dfrac{1}{4} m A^2 \omega^2 [1 + \cos(2\omega t + 2\phi)]$

This shows that the kinetic energy oscillates with an angular frequency $2\omega$, meaning its time period is half that of the pendulum, i.e., $T' = \dfrac{T}{2}$.

The graph in option (3) correctly represents a non-negative oscillating quantity with a period of $T/2$.

Answer:

84618.text: Which of the following depicts the correct pathway of transport of sperms?
options: Rete testis $\to$ Efferent ductules $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Vas deferens
Rete testis $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Efferent ductules $\to$ Vas deferens
Rete testis $\to$ Vas deferens $\to$ Efferent ductules $\to$ Epididymis
Efferent ductules  $\to$  Rete testis  $\to$  Vas deferens  $\to$  Epididymis
84618.sol:
The pathway of transport of sperms in the human male is:

Sperm is manufactured in testes. The epididymis stores the immature sperms received from testes for several days. After ejaculation, sperm is expelled from the epididymis into the deferent duct. The sperm then travels through the deferent duct into the pelvic cavity to the prostate. The vas deferens are connected to the seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct, which passes through the prostate and empties into the urethra.

Seminiferous tubules $\to$ Rete testis $\to$ Vasa efferentia $\to$ Epididymis $\to$ Vas deferens $\to$ Ejaculatory duct $\to$ Urethra $\to$ Urethral meatus

100032.subject: Physics
100032.text: Which of the following statements regarding errors in measurement is incorrect?
options: Systematic errors tend to be in one direction, either positive or negative.
Systematic errors can be estimated and the necessary corrections can be applied to the readings.
Random errors occur irregularly and are unpredictable with respect to sign and size.
Imperfection in experimental procedure or technique always leads to a random error.
100032.sol:
Systematic errors are those that tend to be in one direction, either positive or negative. Because their causes are known, they can often be estimated and necessary corrections can be applied to the readings.

Random errors occur irregularly and are unpredictable with respect to sign and size.

Imperfection in experimental procedure or technique (such as ignoring the buoyancy of air or measuring temperature under the armpit) is a known, consistent flaw that biases the result in a specific direction. Therefore, it is a source of systematic error, not a random error. The statement claiming it leads to a random error is incorrect.

Answer: Imperfection in experimental procedure or technique always leads to a random error.

101385.subject: Physics
101385.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the acceleration due to gravity ($g$) at various positions relative to the earth's surface ($R$ is the radius of the earth).

List-IList-II
P. At a height $h = R$1. $g/9$
Q. At a height $h = 2R$2. $0$
R. At a depth $d = R/2$3. $g/4$
S. At a depth $d = R$4. $g/2$


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
101385.sol:
The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ is given by $g_h = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)^2}$.

For P ($h = R$): $g_h = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + 1\right)^2} = \dfrac{g}{4}$ (Matches with 3)

For Q ($h = 2R$): $g_h = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + 2\right)^2} = \dfrac{g}{9}$ (Matches with 1)

The acceleration due to gravity at a depth $d$ is given by $g_d = g\left(1 - \dfrac{d}{R}\right)$.

For R ($d = \dfrac{R}{2}$): $g_d = g\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{g}{2}$ (Matches with 4)

For S ($d = R$): $g_d = g\left(1 - 1\right) = 0$ (Matches with 2)

The correct matching is P-3, Q-1, R-4, S-2.

Answer: P-3, Q-1, R-4, S-2

101418.subject: Physics
101418.text: A hypothetical planet has an acceleration due to gravity at its surface that is $4$ times that of the Earth, and its radius is half that of the Earth. If the escape velocity on the surface of the Earth is $v_e$, what is the escape velocity on the surface of this hypothetical planet?
101418.sol:
The escape velocity $v$ on the surface of a planet is related to its acceleration due to gravity $g$ and radius $R$ by the formula $v = \sqrt{2gR}$.

For the Earth, $v_e = \sqrt{2g_e R_e}$.

For the hypothetical planet, the acceleration due to gravity is $g_p = 4g_e$ and the radius is $R_p = \dfrac{R_e}{2}$.

The escape velocity on the planet is:
$v_p = \sqrt{2g_p R_p}$

Substituting the given values:
$v_p = \sqrt{2(4g_e)\left(\dfrac{R_e}{2}\right)} = \sqrt{4(g_e R_e)} = \sqrt{2} \sqrt{2g_e R_e} = \sqrt{2} v_e$.

Thus, the escape velocity on the hypothetical planet is $\sqrt{2} v_e$.

Answer: $\sqrt{2} v_e$

101697.subject: Physics
101697.text: A tank contains three immiscible liquids stacked on top of each other. The layers consist of water (density $1\text{ g cm}^{-3}$), an oil (density $0.8\text{ g cm}^{-3}$), and mercury (density $13.6\text{ g cm}^{-3}$), each having a column height of $10\text{ cm}$. What is the height of a pure water column that would exert the exact same hydrostatic pressure at the bottom of the tank?
101697.sol:
The total hydrostatic pressure at the bottom of the tank is the sum of the pressures exerted by each liquid layer.

$P_{\text{total}} = \rho_{\text{water}} g h + \rho_{\text{oil}} g h + \rho_{\text{mercury}} g h$

$P_{\text{total}} = (1 + 0.8 + 13.6) \times g \times 10$

$P_{\text{total}} = 15.4 \times 10 \times g = 154 g$

For an equivalent pure water column of height $H_{\text{equiv}}$:

$P_{\text{water}} = \rho_{\text{water}} g H_{\text{equiv}} = 1 \times g \times H_{\text{equiv}}$

Equating the pressures:

$1 \times g \times H_{\text{equiv}} = 154 g$

$H_{\text{equiv}} = 154\text{ cm}$

Answer: $154\text{ cm}$

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as
Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R$

103478.sol:

Eddy currents are loops of electrical current induced within conductors by a changing magnetic field in the conductor according to Faraday's law of induction. Eddy currents flow in closed loops within conductors, in planes perpendicular to the magnetic field.

Hence, $R$ is the correct explanation and both statements are true.

103602.subject: Physics
103602.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If the number of turns in the coil of a moving coil galvanometer is doubled then the current sensitivity becomes double.

Statement II: Increasing current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer by only increasing the number of turns in the coil will also increase its voltage sensitivity in the same ratio

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement $I$ is true but Statement $II$ is false
Statement $I$ is false but Statement $II$ is true
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are false
Both Statement $I$ and Statement $II$ are true
103602.sol:
For a moving coil galvanometer, 

$\left(NiAB\right) = k\theta$

The current sensitivity is given by 

${S}_{i} = \dfrac{NAB}{k}$

So, if $N$ is doubled then, the current sensitivity is also doubled.

The voltage is given by 

$V = \left(\dfrac{BNA}{Rk}\right)\theta$

The voltage sensitivity is given by

${S}_{v} = \left(\dfrac{NAB}{kR}\right)$

As, $N$ is increased, $R$ also increases. So, the voltage sensitivity does not change as $\dfrac{N}{R}$ remains constant.

103670.subject: Physics
103670.text:
A long solenoid has $5000\text{ turns}$ per metre and carries a current of $2\text{ A}$. An electron is projected from the axis of the solenoid with a velocity of $5 \times 10^5\text{ m/s}$ in a direction perpendicular to the axis. The magnitude of the magnetic force experienced by the electron is:
(Charge of an electron $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$)
103670.sol:
First, calculate the magnetic field inside the long solenoid. The field is uniform and directed parallel to the axis of the solenoid.

$B = \mu_0 n I$

$B = (4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m/A}) \times (5000\text{ m}^{-1}) \times (2\text{ A})$

$B = 4\pi \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}$

Since the electron is projected perpendicular to the axis of the solenoid, the angle $\theta$ between its velocity vector $\vec{v}$ and the magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$ is $90^\circ$.

The magnitude of the magnetic force (Lorentz force) on the electron is given by:

$F = qvB\sin(90^\circ)$

$F = (1.6 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}) \times (5 \times 10^5\text{ m/s}) \times (4\pi \times 10^{-3}\text{ T}) \times 1$

$F = (8.0 \times 10^{-14}) \times (4\pi \times 10^{-3})\text{ N}$

$F = 32\pi \times 10^{-17}\text{ N} = 3.2\pi \times 10^{-16}\text{ N}$

Answer: $3.2\pi \times 10^{-16}\text{ N}$

103816.subject: Physics
103816.text: When a charged particle moving with velocity $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}$ is subjected to a magnetic field of induction $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$, the force on it is non-zero. This implies that
options: angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ can have any value other than $90^{\circ}$
angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ can have any value other than zero and $180^{\circ}$
angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ is either zero or $180^{\circ}$
103816.sol:
When a charged particle $q$ is moving in a uniform magnetic field $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ with velocity $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}$ such that angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ be $\theta$, then due to interaction between the magnetic field produced due to moving charge and magnetic force applied, the charge $q$ experiences a force which is given by
$F=q v B \sin \theta$
If $\theta=0^{\circ}$ or $180^{\circ}$, then $\sin \theta=0$
$\therefore \quad F=q v B \sin \theta=0$
Since, force on charged particle is non-zero, so angle between $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{v}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{B}}$ can have any value other than zero and $180^{\circ}$.
Note : Force experienced by the charged particle is Lorentz force.

104482.subject: Physics
104482.text: A ray of monochromatic light passes through an equilateral prism such that the refracted ray inside the prism is parallel to its base. If the angle of deviation of the ray is $60^\circ$, what is the critical angle of the prism material with respect to air?
104482.sol:
For an equilateral prism, the angle of the prism is $A = 60^\circ$.

The refracted ray is parallel to the base, meaning the prism is in the position of minimum deviation. In this state, the angle of refraction is $r = \dfrac{A}{2} = 30^\circ$.

The angle of deviation is given as $\delta = 60^\circ$. Using the formula for minimum deviation:
$\delta = 2i - A$
$60^\circ = 2i - 60^\circ$
$2i = 120^\circ \Rightarrow i = 60^\circ$

The refractive index of the prism material is:
$\mu = \dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \dfrac{\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 30^\circ} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{\dfrac{1}{2}} = \sqrt{3}$

The critical angle $\theta_c$ of the prism material with respect to air is given by:
$\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{1}{\mu}$
$\sin \theta_c = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
$\theta_c = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$.

Answer: $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$
